Subject: SLA carveout request for our VPC-connected deployment

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for onboarding us onto Redwood Private last month. We have one open item from procurement/legal: Novus operates the VPC and our on-prem networking for the private deployment, and our security team is asking for a narrowly scoped SLA amendment that recognizes customer-controlled network/maintenance windows.

High-level ask: could Redwood agree to an SLA carveout that excludes network interruptions or latency increases caused by Novus-managed infrastructure (e.g., scheduled maintenance on our transit routers, third-party MPLS provider blips, or our planned nightly patch window)? We still want clear uptime and latency commitments for Redwood-managed components (inference runtime, KV cache, etc.), but need mutual language that avoids holding Novus accountable for outages outside our control.

I attached a small network diagram and a short list of our maintenance windows. Procurement copied.

Appreciate a quick confirmation that Redwood can accept a shared-responsibility clause, and any suggested wording you prefer. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lewis
Director, Cloud Ops — Novus Health

Sarah — thanks for the note and the diagram, very helpful. We can accommodate a narrowly scoped carveout; want to align on a clean, testable definition so both sides know when credits/penalties apply. A couple quick clarifying questions: 

- Can you confirm the regular maintenance windows (timezone + CRON-style recurrence is useful)?
- Do you have an existing change advisory board (CAB) or maintenance notice process we should rely on for advance notice?
- For latency: what percentile and thresholds are you most concerned about (p95, p99, >200ms)?

From Redwood's side we'll propose: Redwood-backed uptime/latency SLOs apply to Redwood-managed components and to traffic over properly provisioned/peered VPC paths. We would exclude customer-controlled network incidents where Novus has primary control (with a requirement that Novus provide evidence such as traceroutes/edge provider incident IDs). We'll draft sample legal language and run it by Neha/legal and Marissa for commercial sign-off.

Looping in Marissa (AM) and Neha (Legal) to propose draft amendment language and proposed monitoring / evidence requirements.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: SLA carveout request — draft thoughts

Team — drafting notes for the amendment. High-level commercial stance: we want to preserve uptime credits for Redwood-managed failures while avoiding exposure to customer infra. Proposed commercial guardrails: 

- Attribution clause: Customer disruptions arising from Novus-managed network, third-party ISPs, or transit providers are excluded from credit calculations if Novus provides a post-incident report within 72 hours.
- Latency carveout: If p95 latency degradation is observed and Novus can demonstrate packet loss or path changes inside their network, latency incidents attributed to Novus are excluded.
- Monitoring: Redwood will continue to publish per-route latency and token-level timing; both parties will exchange traces and NetFlow on request.
- Escalation: For incidents with unclear attribution, we propose a 5-business-day investigation window with an independent network forensics vendor if needed. Costs for independent forensics split 50/50 unless Redwood is clearly at fault.

I've attached a short amendment draft to start (proposed-sla-amendment-draft.docx). Marcus — need your ops input on what instrumentation we can reasonably provide in a VPC setup (e.g., synthetic probes, traceroutes, token-level timing). Neha — will need legal language for the evidence and credit calculation parts.

Marissa
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Thanks — I reviewed Marissa's commercial bullets and made suggested legal text. Key elements I want in the amendment: 

1) Clear definitions: 
   - "Redwood-managed components" (runtime, model host, KV cache, control-plane services hosted by Redwood).
   - "Customer-managed network" (Novus-managed VPC, on-prem transit, peering fabric, and named third-party transit providers).

2) Attribution & Evidence: Incident attribution requires (a) Redwood operational logs showing component health, (b) customer evidence (traceroutes, BGP change logs, maintenance ticket IDs). If both sides present conflicting evidence, the parties may escalate to the independent network forensics vendor referenced in the amendment.

3) Credits language: Credits only apply when a majority of impacted requests within a rolling hour are attributable to Redwood-managed failures. If attribution is to Customer-managed network, credits do not apply.

4) Limited exclusion for scheduled maintenance: If Novus provides >=48 hours notice for scheduled network maintenance, Redwood will exclude any resulting downtime/latency from SLA calculations.

5) Temporary operational mitigations: Redwood will offer recommended mitigations (multi-region endpoints, redundancy patterns, local proxy configurations) and will provide configuration verification support during onboarding. Purchase of any additional redundancy is outside the amendment scope.

I can convert this to contract-ready language and initiate an amendment template on DocuSign once Novus confirms these high-level points. Proposed DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/Novus/SLA-Amendment/abcdef123456

-Neha
Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Sarah — thanks for the details and diagram. Per our internal review we've drafted a narrowly scoped amendment that should address Novus' ask while preserving measurable SLOs for Redwood-managed services. Summary of the proposed approach: 

- We will maintain standard uptime/latency SLOs for Redwood-managed components.
- Incidents caused by Novus-managed network (including scheduled maintenance with >=48h notice, third-party transit failures, or changes to peering) will be excluded from SLA calculations provided Novus supplies corroborating evidence within 72 hours.
- For ambiguous incidents we propose a 5-business-day joint investigation and, if needed, independent forensics (cost-sharing described in the amendment).
- Redwood will publish per-route telemetry and work with Novus to instrument synthetic probes at onboarding.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached draft amendment and Novus network diagram.
2) If acceptable, Novus legal can take the DocuSign link (below) to review and redline; otherwise propose a brief call — happy to set up 30 minutes this week.
